assertions.source: D(q₀)=√(Σ_{λ⊢5} d_q²)=11.357 ∉ {8, 8π} (corpus-fixed n=5 data, no scan) => the naive S₀₀=1/D shared-wall identification is falsified on the observable side

description: Self-test of the merged α_EM↔W_λ shared-wall acceptance gate (#3853) against the corpus's OWN fixed modular data — no wait on Front-2's colored-LR, no level scan. KeystoneVerlindeSMatrixBridge fixes D=√(Σ_{λ∈P} d_q(λ)²) with P=partitions of n=5 (McKay/A₅⊂S₅/2I, |S₅|=|2I|=120); d_q = hook-content quantum dimension; observable q₀ ⇒ full untruncated non-unitary set. RESULT: D(q₀)=11.3569 — NEITHER 8 NOR 8π (25.1327); D(1)=√120=10.9545; D/8=1.4196, D/8π=0.4519. So the naive S₀₀=1/D identification FALSIFIES the shared-wall in its literal form: the keystone total quantum dimension D (n=5 partition datum) ≠ the photon count b₁=8 (genus-4 homology) ≠ 8π. α_EM 1/(π b₁) and the W_λ keystone 1/D are DISTINCT normalizations on the observable side. Scope-(a) NEGATIVE (not a structural exclusion): a fibre-side truncated admissible D(ζ) at a root of unity, or a different index route, could still link them. The gate was falsifiable, fed non-tunable corpus data, returned NO. No fit; no α_k wired; 1/(8π) stays a phase-4 identification.

gate_result.verdict: D(q₀)=11.357 ∉ {8,8π} ⇒ shared-wall 'photon b₁ = keystone D' FALSIFIED on the observable side (scope-(a) negative); distinct normalizations

scope.not_excluded: fibre-side truncated admissible D(ζ) at a root of unity (Front-2 colored-LR), or a different index route linking b₁ and the keystone data
